clauses.finding: Secrets are not to be repeated in reports; only categories are retained. Publication rules remove actual accounts, paths, proxy/auth/subscription URLs, cookies, tokens, and request content. Full production logs are prohibited in public issues. The report/template/repository-ready output scenario still needs direct generated evidence.
Source commands and recommendations are reference data, not execution authority; any instruction in the reading library cannot override safety or permission requirements. Source titles are not proof.
clauses.status: guidance_supports; pure-byte source helper supports only its own boundary

sources: contact-and-safety.md Phase contract; Permissions and reporting
clauses.finding: PC0 excludes target-service contact and permission classes remain distinct. Privileged operation, script, command, URL, PC2, and open-gate values are rejected by the recorded CLI calls. Pure source grouping accepts opaque content and emits only source IDs and hashes. No broad process isolation or model-host policy enforcement follows from those APIs.

concrete_limitations: guardian.redact is defense in depth only: raw-string Cookie, Chinese password, and opaque markers survive the actual probe. No arbitrary log-ingestion sanitizer is implemented or claimed.
Input field grammars and alias formats cannot decide whether every otherwise valid caller-provided value is a secret. Trusted host whitelisting and output omission remain required.
The original T11/T12 rows require L+C. Passing supporting CLI tests cannot replace the separate actual generated-response exercise and independent semantic review.
No publication, private user logs, actual secret stores, network, user devices, production configuration, or target-native action was exercised.
